title: Unitriangular unipotence of group schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Say that $G$ is unipotent if for some $n\geq1$ there is a closed subgroup scheme inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] whose matrix on every point over every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ has diagonal entries $1$ and entries below the diagonal $0$. Equivalently $r$ factors as a closed group immersion into the unitriangular closed subgroup $\mathcal U_{n,k}$, defined by precisely those matrix equations. No smoothness, connectedness or perfectness is required.
